ios.desc: I decided to create Pinsets on a trip to New York. I just wanted to draw a box on the map and find recommended pizza places in that area, but no apps worked that way. So, when I got back, I wrote my own. It's so easy now to share a list of ice cream shops, or mailboxes, or pretty murals. I also find it handy around town to keep track of places, even where I parked my car.

show_hn.title: Show HN: My iPhone app for mapping pins

quotes.text:
I wrote a free iPhone app to share recommended places, and to let you place pins more easily:

https://itunes.apple.com/us/app/share-theres/id1438481654?ls=1&mt=8

It's not like Yelp or the built-in map searches because it's centered around the pins more than the themes.
I got the idea on a trip to New York. I just wanted to draw a box on the map within a small 2-block area to see what's there--like recommended pizza places, for example, or to see all the recommended places of any theme, but only within that box.
All the other map/social/share apps keep expanding the boundary, showing you things far beyond the constraints.
This one works exactly the way I always wished the Google map and the Apple map (and Yelp) would work.

You can also keep the "pinsets" stored locally; I find it handy to use for things like where I parked my car, or where I started a walk.
You can send a map pin to someone in the form of a URL, which means you can send it from iPhone to Android or to a desktop computer in a text message.
I know the maps have ways to do this, but I see so many people who struggle with it; they resort to sending a screen capture of the pin's location.
It seemed a clear indicator that the map's UI is overly cluttered and confusing to people.

The backend uses CloudKit storage, so hopefully it will remain free for me to operate. (This is just a hobby project; I'm not trying to turn it into a business or anything.)
